story.head: Faulk meets his old team
paras: The Red Wings have won two in a row, and the Blues (6-6-1) beat Boston 4-1 on Thursday. Going in, the Blues are fifth in the Central (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Wings last in the Atlantic (tied for 16th).

The Blues have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .588, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Red Wings (.577 on chances worth .634), where their finishing has held them back.

The Blues keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (2nd), but have struggled on the power play (31st). The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd) and draw more penalties than they take (2nd). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (3rd), and their power play against the Blues’ penalty killers is strength against strength. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Dylan Holloway (3 G / 8 A / 11 P in 13 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, and Jimmy Snuggerud (7 G / 2 A / 9 P in 13 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Red Wings, Alex DeBrincat (6 G / 9 A / 15 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with four goals in six games against St. Louis since 2023-24. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with nine points in his last five games.
Joel Hofer (5-3-1 / .923 SV% in 9 GS) has been a rock in net for St. Louis and is expected to start. John Gibson (4-4-1 / .874 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to go for Detroit.
